parts.display_text: An object of mass 2m, initially moving at 3v, sticks to a stationary object of mass 4m. Their common final speed is v. Determine the loss of total kinetic energy.

answer.text: Initial energy = ½(2m)(3v)² = 9mv². Final energy = ½(6m)v² = 3mv². The loss is 6mv².

sup-064316255265a882-0HL1q5:whole.hint: The spring force changes as the spring stretches. How is that represented on a force–extension graph?
notes: For a Hooke’s-law spring, F = kx and elastic energy = ½kx². Here x is extension or compression from the natural length.
When spring, kinetic and gravitational energy all change, include all three stores. Do not use F_final x for the spring’s work.

sup-064316255265a882-0HL1q6:whole.hint: Calculate the total kinetic energy before and after, using the supplied velocities or momentum result.
notes: Add ½mv² for every moving object in each state. Energy dissipated is initial kinetic energy minus final kinetic energy.
Use E_k = p²/(2m) when momentum is supplied. Do not assume equal momenta imply equal kinetic energies for different masses.

sup-064316255265a882-0HL1q7:whole.hint: Decide whether the question asks for energy over an interval or the rate of transfer at one instant.
notes: Average power is energy transferred / time. Instantaneous mechanical power is P = Fv cos θ.
With a constant driving force, power still changes when speed changes. With constant power, driving force decreases as speed increases.
